recentItems.title: China's Brain-computer Interface Sector Enters Fast Track
recentItems.description:
China's brain-computer interface industry is entering the fast lane with continuous tech breakthroughs and expanded application scenarios.

With rapid advances in neural recording, neuromodulation, and signal decoding, BCI technology is opening new opportunities for treating things like paralysis from spinal cord injuries, strokes or Parkinson's disease.

The BCI sector was designated a future industry in this year's government work report. It was also included in the outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan as the country aims to cultivate it into a new engine of growth.

The China Academy of Information and Communications Technology expects China's BCI market to be valued at 1.8 billion U.S. dollars by 2030.

recentItems.title: Chinese Scientists Give Dinosaur Egg Site 'Heart Checkup' Scan with Electrical Imaging
recentItems.description:
Scientists in central China's Hubei Province are using non-invasive electrical imaging to explore an archeological site, giving it what amounts to an EKG.

At the Qinglongshan Dinosaur Egg Fossil Group National Nature Reserve, home to the world's largest collection of preserved dinosaur eggs, researchers lay cables and place electrode arrays on the ground.

In establishing an artificial electric field with underground currents, the team can measure how different rock and sediment layers conduct electricity, allowing them to reconstruct the surface geology in detail.

The park has some 3,000 fossilized dinosaur eggs and has achieved large scale, intact conservation of the eggs in their original setting.

Over the years, surface laser scanning and other work has been carried out, but underground exploration has been challenging because traditional drilling risks damaging the fossils.

The scientists say the findings will help them reconstruct the region's ancient geography and ecology and unlock new clues about life during the Cretaceous period.
